pr_title: Fix the flaky kubectl tests at scale
pr_body:
Fix #87851 

waitForPod is build on top of informer framework with is initialized from apiserver watch cache which doesn't have a guarantee to be up-to-date. In large clusters, where we observe small hundreds of milliseconds delays, the tests are flaky, because the informer is initialized without having the pod in it and the initial precondition is failing.

```release-note
NONE
```

> @soltysh - thoughts? ^^

I think the problem is with this condition https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/run/run.go#L385 and the follow-up exit condition when we are waiting for a pod: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/run/run.go#L387

I think we should have two distinct conditions, for `RestartPolicyNever` `podCompleted` is fine b/c it waits for either Failure or Success of the pod, as one would expect. With `RestartPolicyOnFailure` the expectation is that the pod will only succeed, so we'd need a different exit condition. Lemme put together a fix on top of yours.

OK - I think I know what is going on here.
Here is what is happening (for the test case from two comments above):
- the test is setting "-i", so interactive mode is switched on
- that option triggers that Attach option defaults to true: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/run/run.go#L187
- over the Run() command, we get to the handleAttachPod: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/run/run.go#L378
- handleAttachPod is calling waitForPod

And waitForPod is broken.
The problem is the preconditionFunc: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/run/run.go#L460
which is below passed to the UntilWithSync function

UntilWithSync underneath is creating an informer and calling that function against its state:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/watch/until.go#L143

But the informer is initialized from apiserver watchcache, so it may be lagging.
In large clusters we are observing lags in the order of small hundreds of milliseconds and that seem to be enough.

What is happening is that:
- informer is initialized (but the pod creation is not yet reflected in it)
- the preconditionFunc is called
- the state doesn't contain that pod (yet)
- the whole thing fails with that error

I actually believe, that just removing the preconditionFunc should actually solve the problem. I opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90417 for that.
